blocks.x: Data & Lakehouse applied to Property & Casualty. This page sets out the operating context, the delivery pattern we run, the services and platforms involved, and the outcomes we commit to.

P&C economics live in two moments: pricing the risk before the event and handling the claim after it. Both are decision factories — rate against exposure and catastrophe models, settle against policy language and fraud signals — and both reward carriers whose document and data machinery is industrialized.

items: Underwriting exposure and claims experience never meet; portfolio steering is retrospective.
FNOL, estimates, medical and police files arrive as documents; triage takes days and leakage hides in the queue.

blocks.x: The pattern composes Lakehouse Architecture & Migration, Real-Time Streaming & Event-Driven Decisioning, Data Engineering & Pipeline Modernization from the Data, Analytics & Lakehouse tower, wired into the unit's workflows (FNOL and claims triage, Estimate review and leakage control, Commercial risk surveying) on Dataq Forge and Dataq Nexus. Governance inherits the sector frame — Rate filing regimes among others — with evidence generated by the delivery itself.

items: Turn the data estate into revenue: embedded analytics, data sharing and insight products with real P&L.
Resilient, observable pipelines: trusted data from source to decision at SLA.
Lakehouse the right way: Unity Catalog governance, cost-aware design and AI-ready foundations.
Exposure + claims unified with lineage for actuaries (steering analytics real)

blocks.x: At industry level, the same pattern

At Insurance & Risk level this capability reads as: triangle pipelines, chain-ladder and ML hybrids with actuarial-in-command controls (reserve review cycles shortened materially). The sub-industry page narrows it to the unit's workflows, regimes and KPIs.

Programs run on a fixed rhythm so progress is visible from week one. Weeks 1–2 lock the baseline: the current metric is measured with your team and signed before build starts. Weeks 3–8 deliver the pilot on bounded scope — one decision path, one workflow, one plant or one portfolio — with a control owner named on your side. Weeks 9–12 industrialize what worked: runbooks, monitoring, enablement and a measured delta against the signed baseline. Anything that misses its gate is stopped or redirected with a documented decision, not quietly extended.
